content: The metabolism of the intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 can be affected by various drugs, leading to significant interactions. Below are detailed descriptions of these interactions and their clinical implications: 1. Pexidartinib and CYP3A4 Inhibitors: Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors can increase pexidartinib levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, the pexidartinib dose should be reduced as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the original pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 2. Phenobarbital and Tetracycline: Phenobarbital decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 3. Phenytoin and Tetracycline: Phenytoin reduces tetracycline levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or consider an alternative therapy. 4. Metronidazole and Pimozide: Metronidazole increases pimozide levels by inhibiting its metabolism, which is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 5. Polysaccharide Iron and Tetracycline: Polysaccharide iron reduces tetracycline absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Primidone and Tetracycline: Primidone decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 7. Metronidazole and Propylene Glycol: This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of a disulfiram-like reaction. 8. Metronidazole and Ranolazine: Metronidazole increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 9. Tetracycline and Rapacuronium: Tetracycline enhances the effects of rapacuronium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 10. Metronidazole and Repotrectinib: Metronidazole increases repotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Tetracycline and Rocuronium: Tetracycline enhances the effects of rocuronium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Selinexor and Metronidazole: Co-administration may lead to neurological toxicities. Avoid combining selinexor with medications that cause dizziness or confusion. 13. Rose Hips and Tetracycline: Rose hips reduce tetracycline absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Tetracycline and Selumetinib: Tetracycline increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose as per the drug monograph. 15. Metronidazole and Silodosin: Metronidazole increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Tetracycline and Siponimod: Tetracycline increases siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with CYP2C9 inhibitors. 17. Metronidazole and Simvastatin: Metronidazole increases simvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Tetracycline and Succinylcholine: Tetracycline enhances the effects of succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 19. Metronidazole and Tazemetostat: Metronidazole increases tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Tetracycline and Temocillin: Tetracycline reduces the effects of temocillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 21. Bismuth Subsalicylate and Tetracycline: Bismuth subsalicylate reduces tetracycline absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 22. Metronidazole and Tolvaptan: Metronidazole increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. Tetracycline and Tretinoin: Tetracycline increases the risk of phototoxicity when combined with tretinoin due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Tetracycline and Tripotassium Dicitratobismuthate: This combination reduces tetracycline absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Tetracycline and Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Tetracycline reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Metronidazole and Venetoclax: Metronidazole increases venetoclax levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for toxicities. 27. Bismuth Subsalicylate and Warfarin: Bismuth subsalicylate enhances the anticoagulant effects of warfarin. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 28. Tetracycline and Acalabrutinib: Tetracycline increases acalabrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Metronidazole and Alprazolam: Metronidazole increases alprazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Metronidazole and Amiodarone: Metronidazole increases amiodarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Metronidazole and Aprepitant: Metronidazole increases aprepitant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Metronidazole and Aripiprazole: Metronidazole increases aripiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Metronidazole and Atorvastatin: Metronidazole increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Tetracycline and Avanafil: Tetracycline increases avanafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Tetracycline and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Tetracycline reduces the levels of these hormones by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. 36. Metronidazole and Clopidogrel: Metronidazole reduces clopidogrel activation by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Metronidazole and Clozapine: Metronidazole increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Metronidazole and Conivaptan: Metronidazole increases conivaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Metronidazole and Cyclosporine: Metronidazole increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Tetracycline and Cefdinir: Tetracycline reduces cefdinir efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Metronidazole and Diazepam: Metronidazole increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Tetracycline and Didanosine: Didanosine reduces tetracycline absorption. Avoid simultaneous administration and separate doses by at least four hours. 43. Metronidazole and Digoxin: Metronidazole increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Efavirenz and Tetracycline: Efavirenz reduces tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Elagolix and Tetracycline: Elagolix reduces tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
